dashboard.label: About
dashboard.description: Technical reference, data model, operation semantics, searches, setup and licensing for Log Source Watch.

div.div: LOG SOURCE WATCH — TECHNICAL REFERENCE
div.h1: Architecture, data flow and operational behavior
div.p: This page documents the runtime behavior of Log Source Watch 4.9.3: source identity, KV Store collections, management actions, discovery and enrollment, scheduled searches, reports, first-run setup and licensing.

Log Source Watch monitors expected log continuity at index + host granularity. The canonical source state is based on the monitored stream itself; optional _internal correlation adds diagnostic evidence about recent Splunk activity for the same host without redefining host uptime.
div.div: Authoritative configuration: lsw_inventory. Latest observation: lsw_lastseen. Optional Splunk heartbeat evidence: lsw_heartbeat. Materialized operational state: lsw_state. Administrative history: lsw_audit.
div.p: The Overview and Management workspaces calculate the effective state directly from inventory + last_seen for immediate UI consistency and add heartbeat diagnosis when matching lsw_heartbeat evidence exists. LSW_Build_State periodically materializes the same canonical state and diagnostics into lsw_state for reports and exports.
The immutable source key is generated as sha256(index."|".host). The same host name in different customer or application indexes therefore remains a distinct monitored source.

ol.li: status="maintenance" and maintenance_until=0 or a future epoch → MAINTENANCE.
No last_seen value → NO LOG OBSERVATION.

pre.code: definition = eval threshold_seconds=coalesce(threshold_seconds,7200), threshold_minutes=round(threshold_seconds/60,0), maintenance_until=coalesce(maintenance_until,0), age_seconds=if(isnull(last_seen),null(),now()-last_seen), age_minutes=if(isnull(age_seconds),null(),round(age_seconds/60,1)) | eval effective_state=case(status=="retired","RETIRED",status=="maintenance" AND (maintenance_until=0 OR maintenance_until>now()),"MAINTENANCE",isnull(last_seen),"NO LOG OBSERVATION",age_seconds>threshold_seconds,"SILENT",true(),"OK") | eval alarm=if(effective_state=="SILENT",1,0) iseval = 0

div.div: Freshness clock: source age is based on the event timestamp _time, not Splunk index time _indextime. LSW_Update_LastSeen stores latest(_time) for each registered index + host, and state calculation uses now() - last_seen. Delayed/backfilled events with old event timestamps therefore do not make a source appear freshly reporting merely because they were indexed recently.

div.div: Units: thresholds are entered in whole minutes in Management, Bulk Actions and Discovery. They are stored as integer seconds in threshold_seconds. The UI supports 1–10080 minutes (1 minute to 7 days).
div.p: The tables below explain the application fields whose names are technical or whose units/semantics are not obvious from the name alone. Epoch fields are Unix timestamps in seconds unless stated otherwise.

details.summary: Common source identity and policy fields

tr.td: Stable source identity: sha256(index."|".host). The same host name in two indexes is therefore two independent monitored sources.
Splunk index that contains events for the monitored source.
The event host value that identifies the source inside the selected index.
Configured lifecycle state. Valid values are active, maintenance and retired. This is policy, not the live operational state.
Maximum allowed silence before an ACTIVE source becomes SILENT. Operators enter whole minutes; the KV Store stores integer seconds.
End of a timed maintenance window. 0 means maintenance remains active until an operator explicitly clears it.

Machine-readable provenance tag describing which application action most recently changed the policy. It is not a unique transaction ID. Examples: ui-threshold, ui-maintenance, ui-maintenance-clear, ui-activate, ui-retire, ui-bulk-*, ui-discovery-enroll, setup-initial-enrollment and maintenance-expired. Audit Trail converts these raw values to the human-readable Origin column.
Time when the source inventory document was first created.
Time when that KV Store document was last updated by Log Source Watch.
Latest event _time observed for the registered index + host source.
Timestamp copied from lsw_lastseen.updated_at; tells when the last-seen record itself was refreshed.
now() - last_seen. Null when no log observation exists.
Canonical live state after precedence rules: RETIRED, MAINTENANCE, NO LOG OBSERVATION, SILENT or OK.
Binary export/helper flag. 1 only when effective_state="SILENT"; otherwise 0.
Time when the materialized canonical state row was last calculated.
Time the administrative action was recorded.
Splunk user that initiated the action.
Action surface: for example manage, bulk or enrollment.
Action type: source_enrolled, threshold_change, maintenance_set or lifecycle_change.
Lifecycle value before and after the action.
Silence threshold before and after the action.
Maintenance expiry before and after the action; 0 represents “until cleared”.
Raw provenance tag from the changed source policy. The report presents a friendlier Origin label instead of exposing this internal tag as the primary UI field.
Human-readable explanation of the administrative change.
Name of the monitored application component or scheduled job.
Splunk search job identifier when a search job is associated with the health row.
Component/application version recorded by the health integration.
Time when the health document was last written.

div.p: The Overview risk profile is an early-warning visualization derived from the same event-time age and per-source threshold used by canonical state. It does not introduce new lifecycle or alarm states.

tr.td: Less than half of the configured silence budget has been consumed.
The source is still healthy but has consumed 50–80% of its silence threshold.
The source remains healthy but is close to becoming SILENT. At exactly 100% the source is still OK because SILENT begins only when age is greater than the threshold.
The configured silence threshold has been exceeded.
The registered source has not yet produced a stored observation.

div.div: Scope: MAINTENANCE and RETIRED sources are excluded from the risk bands. Watch and Near threshold are visualization categories only; they do not create alerts, change effective_state, or alter the Silent Sources export.

div.p: The top-level Management view is one workspace with four internal tabs: Sources, Bulk Actions, Discover and Initial Setup. Sources and Bulk Actions read and write application KV Store directly through Splunk's authenticated application service. The page does not require a browser reload after a successful policy change.

tr.td: State derives from current last_seen and threshold.
Source returns to last-seen collection scope.
LSW_Expire_Maintenance returns expired windows to active.
Expiry job intentionally leaves it unchanged.

div.div: Audit ordering: Management reads recent per-source audit entries through KV Store REST using sort=event_time_epoch:-1. The Audit Trail report presents change_ref as a human-readable Origin value while the raw provenance tag remains stored in KV Store.
Bulk safety: Bulk Actions enforces a hard maximum of 10,000 affected sources per operation. The filtered scope is reviewed before changes are applied.

div.p: Discovery is operator-driven. No broad event search is dispatched merely by opening the page. The operator chooses an index and lookback window and starts the scan.

pre.code: | tstats latest(_time) AS observed_last_seen count AS events WHERE index="<selected index>" earliest=<lookback> latest=now BY index host | where len(host)>0 AND len(host)<=255 | eval _key=sha256(index."|".host) | lookup local=true lsw_inventory _key OUTPUT status AS existing_status | where isnull(existing_status)

div.p: The lookup comparison means only source identities missing from lsw_inventory are shown as NEW.

ul.li: lsw_inventory: new source becomes status="active" with the selected whole-minute threshold and change_ref="ui-discovery-enroll".
lsw_lastseen: seeded from observed_last_seen returned by the discovery search.
lsw_state: canonical state is calculated immediately so the source is visible without waiting for the scheduled rebuild.
lsw_audit: one source_enrolled document per enrolled source with scope="enrollment".

div.div: Enroll All safety: enrollment is capped at 10,000 sources. The application performs a fresh read-only discovery query before an all-source enrollment.

Splunk query confirmation warnings: Splunk can require confirmation before packaged administrative searches or custom commands run. Accept the warning only when you intentionally initiated the corresponding Log Source Watch action. This is expected for protected write workflows and does not mean the packaged search is failing.
div.p: On a clean installation app.conf has is_configured=0 and setup_view=initial_setup. Splunk therefore directs the administrator to Initial Setup before normal use.

ol.li: KV Store collections and lookup definitions are loaded from the packaged schema.
The administrator selects the first index, baseline lookback and default threshold.
Setup discovers index + host pairs and writes lsw_inventory.
Setup verifies Inventory / LastSeen / State counts and then marks the app configured.

div.p: Before enrollment, Application Health reports WAITING FOR SETUP / NOT INITIALIZED instead of treating an intentionally empty installation as an operational outage.
Recurring jobs are enabled in the package and staggered across the five-minute cycle. Source state remains based on the monitored stream; heartbeat collection only enriches diagnosis.

tr.td: Refreshes the latest event observation for active and maintenance index + host sources.
Collects latest index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd source=*splunkd.log evidence for monitored host names over a 30-minute dispatch window.
Returns expired timed maintenance sources to active state and writes an audit event.
Materializes canonical source state plus heartbeat diagnostics into lsw_state.
Exports silent sources including heartbeat and diagnosis fields.
Exports scheduler and KV Store health.

div.div: Fail-closed setup behavior: source and heartbeat searches use the registered inventory to build their scope. Before enrollment, a sentinel value prevents an unconfigured search from scanning arbitrary hosts or indexes.
Heartbeat is optional diagnostic context: an empty lsw_heartbeat collection is not an application-health failure. Agentless sources can legitimately have no matching _internal telemetry.

div.p: Log Source Watch correlates monitored hosts with recent index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd source=*splunkd.log activity. This is diagnostic evidence only: it does not change the canonical lifecycle state or automatically assume every source is Universal Forwarder-based.

tr.td: The monitored data stream is silent while Splunk internal telemetry for the same host is still current. Investigate input/log production/parsing/routing before host availability.
Both the monitored stream and Splunk internal heartbeat are stale. Investigate forwarder/service/host/connectivity first.
No recent matching _internal evidence is available. This is normal for agentless sources and must not be treated as proof that a host is down.

div.div: Default heartbeat freshness: 15 minutes via lsw_heartbeat_stale_seconds. The heartbeat scheduler searches only monitored host names and stores the latest evidence in lsw_heartbeat.

tr.td: Human-readable dark report of currently silent sources.
Scheduler freshness, KV Store readiness, monitoring statistics and _internal heartbeat diagnostics.
Filterable administrative history. Legacy scope="add" rows are normalized to enrollment in the report UI.
Machine-readable saved search containing every source whose canonical effective_state is currently SILENT, including heartbeat and diagnosis fields.
Persisted machine-readable silent-source snapshot recalculated from current inventory, last-seen and heartbeat data on its scheduled export cycle.

div.div: Current-state consistency: Overview, Management, Silent Sources, Application Health source statistics and the LSW_SilentHost backend search calculate current state from lsw_inventory + lsw_lastseen + lsw_heartbeat with the shared lsw_calculate_state macro. They do not wait for the periodic lsw_state materialization before a threshold crossing becomes visible. lsw_state remains the persisted canonical snapshot built by LSW_Build_State.

Operational integration: an external monitoring or workflow system can query LSW_SilentHost or consume lsw_silent_hosts.csv. A non-empty current SILENT list is suitable for opening an investigation workflow. The exported heartbeat_status, diagnosis and diagnosis_label fields provide first-step triage context. Planned work should be placed in MAINTENANCE so it is not exported as SILENT.

Important: NO LOG OBSERVATION is intentionally separate from SILENT and is not included in LSW_SilentHost. If an operational process must also react to newly enrolled sources that have never been observed, monitor that state separately.

div.p: Source-controlled application configuration belongs under app/logsource_watch/default/. Do not modify installed defaults for environment-specific production configuration.
Deployment-specific configuration belongs under $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/logsource_watch/local/ or the corresponding Search Head Cluster deployer app local/ directory.
Management, Bulk Actions, Discover, Initial Setup and Audit Trail are restricted to admin / sc_admin in packaged metadata.
The monitoring overview, Silent Sources and Application Health are read-only operational views.

div.div: Community Edition: Log Source Watch may be used free of charge for personal, internal and commercial use for the licensee's own operations with up to 100 Monitored Sources. A Monitored Source is one unique index + host combination whose lifecycle status is active or maintenance. retired sources do not count toward licensed capacity.
div.p: A paid Log Source Watch commercial license is required for more than 100 Monitored Sources, Splunk Search Head Cluster deployment, multiple production search heads, MSP/MSSP or other managed/hosted service use, and redistribution/resale/bundling. Paid editions may include Professional, Enterprise, Enterprise Plus and Service Provider entitlements.
div.div: Standalone capacity extension: organizations that exceed the standard Professional source capacity but do not need Search Head Cluster or multiple-production deployment rights may request a separately signed Professional capacity extension. Enterprise is intended to represent a meaningful scale or topology step, not an arbitrary one-source threshold.

Current environment status: runtime license validity, monitored-source usage, customer, license ID, expiry and deployment entitlements are shown on the dedicated Licensing page. Application Health also exposes the active edition as operational context.
div.p: On a standalone deployment, an administrator can upload a signed lsw_license.json from the Licensing page. The server validates product identity, signature, validity period and capacity before replacing the active entitlement. Invalid uploads do not replace the current license. A successful replacement is written atomically and the previous file is retained as lsw_license.json.previous.
On Search Head Cluster deployments, license-file upload from an individual member is intentionally disabled; deploy the entitlement consistently through the supported cluster deployment process.
The edition names describe the standard commercial model. A signed license file is authoritative for paid capacity and deployment rights.

tr.td: Single standalone Splunk environment; own operations; no SHC, managed-service or redistribution rights.
One production environment by default. SHC, multiple production environments, managed-service use and redistribution are not included unless explicitly granted.
SHC and multiple production environments can be entitled. Managed-service and redistribution rights remain separate signed entitlements.
Custom capacity and deployment scope. Managed-service and redistribution rights remain separately controlled.
MSP/MSSP/hosted-service use and multi-environment rights can be granted. Redistribution/OEM/bundling remains separate unless explicitly enabled.

div.div: Pricing: the prices above are standard annual public list prices for direct licensing and exclude VAT where applicable. Final capacity, deployment rights, support scope, procurement terms, discounts and renewal terms are defined by the applicable order or commercial agreement. Current public pricing is published at https://logsourcewatch.com/#pricing.

No paid license file is required for Community Edition. When local/lsw_license.json is absent, Log Source Watch operates automatically with a 100 Monitored Source capacity. Existing monitoring is not disabled when capacity is exceeded; actions that would add licensed capacity are blocked.
div.p: Paid entitlements are represented by a cryptographically signed license file installed as $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/logsource_watch/local/lsw_license.json. The app contains only the public verification key. The private issuer key must never be distributed with the app or stored on a production search head.

When capacity is reached, existing registered sources continue to be monitored. Operations that would consume additional capacity — such as discovery enrollment, activating a retired source, or placing a retired source into maintenance — are blocked until capacity is available or a suitable paid license is installed.

When a valid paid license expires, existing registered sources continue to be monitored. Log Source Watch blocks actions that would increase monitored-source capacity until a renewed license is installed. Overview raises an expiry warning during the final 30 days and Application Health shows the exact runtime status.

tr.td: Read-only license status command. Verifies the signed file with the public RSA key embedded in the app and returns edition, capacity, validity, deployment rights and status.
Server-side capacity guard helper for search-based mutation workflows. Initial Setup and the interactive management workspaces perform their own license check before authenticated KV Store writes.
Interactive write paths check license capacity before an action can increase the number of ACTIVE or MAINTENANCE sources.
Optional signed paid entitlement. When absent, Community Edition applies automatically with a 100-source capacity.

div.p: The bundled LICENSE.txt is authoritative. A separately executed commercial agreement supersedes the bundled terms only to the extent stated in that agreement. Log Source Watch is independently developed and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Splunk Inc.
